entries.name: Arctic Creeper
entries.description: A low, gray-stemmed creeper grows among cold, high rocks. Its dried leaves can be used in common poisons that change damage to cold or necrotic.

entries.name: Blueleaf
entries.description: Hardy trees with gleaming blue leaves withstand heavy snow and wind. Their durable wood is prized by northern craftsfolk; burning chips gives blue flames and can yield vivid blue dye.

entries.name: Kanishta
entries.description: A low, cold-climate creeper with broad, soft leaves and a thick, dark root beneath the soil.

entries.name: Obaddis Leaf
entries.description: A rare holly-like leaf retains magic when used as a druidic focus. It can amplify the area and duration of spells that target plants.

entries.name: Salamander Orchid
entries.description: This orchid burns continually. With herbalism tools, its pollen can be prepared for a blade to deal extra fire damage; handling it without proper tools is hazardous.

entries.name: Basilisk Breath
entries.description: A small evergreen with pale berries. Their juice can be prepared as a potent paralytic poison.

entries.name: Cat's Tail
entries.description: A slender coastal plant with spear-shaped leaves and a single flower stalk. Its ground leaves make a salve for sore feet.

entries.name: Dragonwort
entries.description: This gnarled herb has wavy leaves and clustered pink flowers. Its root is used in a long-boiled infusion traditionally given during outbreaks of plague.

entries.name: Air Plant
entries.description: A sponge-like plant stores air; a piece held in the mouth provides several minutes of breathing before it wilts.

entries.name: Sand Vine
entries.description: A rope-like seaweed grows above and below warm coastal water. It can be dried as cordage or processed into a topical anesthetic oil.

entries.name: Ecru
entries.description: Small red-leaved palms form red crystals from built-up resin. The crystal dissolves in strong acid and is used for a brief, blissful respite.

entries.name: Chromus Slime
entries.description: A yellow-orange slime mold thrives in damp places. It filters salt from water and can reverse the effect of a potion or poison when properly combined.

entries.name: Sandberry Bush
entries.description: A remote desert shrub bears small yellow berries. Their tea is used as a gentle sleep aid.

entries.name: Bloodstaunch
entries.description: A bright-leaved herb with a faint honey-and-rain scent grows in dry gullies. Its resin is applied to bleeding wounds.

entries.name: Rose Campion
entries.description: This green-brown herb is taken to guard against scorpion and spider stings.

entries.name: Arrowroot
entries.description: A woody-stemmed desert plant has shallow roots that rise into a small teepee-like structure. Its dried stem is ground into a polishing oil.

entries.name: Ephedra
entries.description: A small succulent bears clusters of leaves that can be dried and ground into a healing poultice or potion additive.

entries.name: Dragontears
entries.description: A translucent desert succulent yields milky sap. A carefully prepared unguent promotes rapid healing; incorrect preparation can be deadly.

entries.name: Bloodgrass
entries.description: A red-veined grass can be ground into a paste and mixed into food or drink as a day's rations.

entries.name: Blueleaf
entries.description: Hardy trees with gleaming blue leaves withstand heavy snow and wind. Their durable wood is prized by northern craftsfolk; burning chips gives blue flames and can yield vivid blue dye.

entries.name: Weirwood Bark
entries.description: A towering, sacred tree has silver-brown leaves and velvet-dark undersides. Its wood resists ordinary fire and is valued for a clear tone in instruments.

entries.name: Golden Lungwort
entries.description: A foot-high herb bears spotted leaves and bell-shaped flowers that shift from pink to blue. It eases aches, though it can impair Intelligence checks for a time.

entries.name: Darkberry
entries.description: A sparse bush bears a few purple berries rich in shadowstuff. Crushing one creates a brief sphere of magical darkness.

entries.name: Kingsfruit
entries.description: A summer-flowering tree produces hard-rinded, sweet golden fruit in autumn. Eating it restores vitality and spent Hit Dice.

entries.name: Fairy Bells
entries.description: Clusters of violet flowers ring as their seeds rattle in the breeze. The flowers are said to repel fiends, who must resist fear to approach.

entries.name: Devilweed
entries.description: Sharp-awned grass can be rolled and smoked, briefly improving Strength checks while hindering other ability checks.

entries.name: Bloodgrass
entries.description: A red-veined grass can be ground into a paste and mixed into food or drink as a day's rations.

entries.name: Fleshwort
entries.description: A short, gray-stemmed plant with hairy leaves thrives where the dead were buried. Healers use its fibrous body to aid recovery during a short rest.

entries.name: Lusiri Blossom
entries.description: A herb with dull red, lip-shaped leaves. Ingestion brings vivid hallucinations and an urge to undertake a distant spirit quest.

entries.name: Ecru
entries.description: Small red-leaved palms form red crystals from built-up resin. The crystal dissolves in strong acid and is used for a brief, blissful respite.

entries.name: Bloodstaunch
entries.description: A bright-leaved herb with a faint honey-and-rain scent grows in dry gullies. Its resin is applied to bleeding wounds.

entries.name: Goblinberry Bush
entries.description: A dark-leaved highland bush bears sharp-smelling reddish-purple berries. Their juice is used in a pungent drink or as an astringent.

entries.name: Arctic Creeper
entries.description: A low, gray-stemmed creeper grows among cold, high rocks. Its dried leaves can be used in common poisons that change damage to cold or necrotic.

entries.name: Ephedra
entries.description: A small succulent bears clusters of leaves that can be dried and ground into a healing poultice or potion additive.

entries.name: Seregon
entries.description: Blood-red flowers grow directly from their roots in rocky soil. Their nectar grants a short-lived reserve of vitality.

entries.name: Basilisk Breath
entries.description: A small evergreen with pale berries. Their juice can be prepared as a potent paralytic poison.

entries.name: Goblin-Trap
entries.description: Leathery, ground-hugging plants conceal golden seed pods behind inward-pointing spines that can trap a careless hand.

entries.name: Creeping Mangrove
entries.description: A gnarled mangrove grows along brackish swamp edges. Its roots slowly shift toward wetter ground, and its wood burns even when soaked.

entries.name: Rattlestalks
entries.description: Tall swamp stalks hold hard seed bulbs that rattle in the wind. Local folk turn them into noisemakers that can frighten the unwary.

entries.name: Corpsebomb
entries.description: A fungus that colonizes damp tissue forms a gas-filled spore sack. When ignited, the sack bursts in a dangerous spray of fire and spores.

entries.name: Knitbone
entries.description: A tall, purple-flowered plant has hard, sharp leaves. Ground leaves and flowers are made into a healing poultice.

entries.name: Tekkil
entries.description: A swamp succulent with thick red leaves has analgesic and euphoric effects, but also makes Dexterity saves more difficult.

entries.name: Fleshwort
entries.description: A short, gray-stemmed plant with hairy leaves thrives where the dead were buried. Healers use its fibrous body to aid recovery during a short rest.

entries.name: Gravefist
entries.description: A pale mushroom with five knobby protrusions resembles a skeletal hand reaching up from the soil. Its spores are feared in dark cellars.

entries.name: Corpsebomb
entries.description: A fungus that colonizes damp tissue forms a gas-filled spore sack. When ignited, the sack bursts in a dangerous spray of fire and spores.

entries.name: Quicksilver Lichen
entries.description: A glittering silver lichen can be ground into a flavorless powder that wards against poison for a short time.

entries.name: Ghost Tendrils
entries.description: A pale fungus spreads tendrils through recent corpses and can animate them imperfectly. It avoids sunlight and is often found in crypts and caves.

entries.name: Wispstalks
entries.description: A rare cave fungus has a translucent blue cap. Proper preparation can make a creature transparent for a short time without making it invisible.
